Medical necessity indications.Guideline Category: Protease Inhibitor Typing or SERPINA1 Targeted Mutation Analysis
Required findings: Abnormally low (less than 120mg/dL) or borderline (90-140mg/dL) alpha-1 antitrypsin (AAT) levels
Symptomatic adults with emphysema, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), or asthma with airflow obstruction that is incompletely reversible after aggressive treatment with bronchodilators
Individuals of any age with unexplained liver disease (including obstructive liver disease in infancy)
Asymptomatic individuals with persistent obstruction on pulmonary function tests who have identifiable risk factors (e.g., cigarette smoking, occupational exposure)
Siblings of an individual with AATD
Rendering laboratory is a qualified provider of service per the Health Plan policy
Medical necessity indications.Source: Test Specific Guidelines > Alpha-1 Antitrypsin Deficiency Testing > Criteria (TOC: S3.2.1)

Required findings: Discrepancies between clinical presentation, serum alpha-1 antitrypsin quantification, targeted mutation analysis, and/or PI typing
Suspected presence of rare variants or null alleles (which cannot be identified by other methods)
Rendering laboratory is a qualified provider of service per the Health Plan policy
Medical necessity indications.Source: Test Specific Guidelines > Alpha-1 Antitrypsin Deficiency Testing > Criteria (TOC: S3.2.1)

Non-Indications: Individuals with normal alpha-1 antitrypsin (AAT) levels (greater than 140mg/dL) who do not meet the specific clinical criteria for PI typing or targeted mutation analysis

Individuals with AAT levels between 120mg/dL and 140mg/dL who do not have symptomatic emphysema/COPD/asthma with incompletely reversible obstruction, unexplained liver disease, persistent obstruction with risk factors, C-ANCA positive vasculitis, necrotizing panniculitis, or are not siblings of an AATD patient

Requests for SERPINA1 sequence analysis without documented discrepancies between clinical presentation, serum AAT quantification, targeted mutation analysis, or PI typing, and without suspicion of rare variants or null alleles
Testing performed by a laboratory that is not a qualified provider of service per the Health Plan policy
Important criteria & exceptions: The inclusion of any procedure code in the guideline table does not imply that the code is under management or requires prior authorization; refer to the specific Health Plan's procedure code list for management requirements
Protease Inhibitor (PI) typing cannot detect null alleles

Targeted mutation analysis identifies common and/or recurring mutations but may have differing clinical sensitivities dependent upon ethnicity, phenotypic presentation, or other case-specific characteristics
Sequence analysis is indicated to identify rare variants or null alleles that would otherwise be missed by PI typing or targeted mutation analysis
Documentation required: Serum alpha-1 antitrypsin (AAT) quantification results showing levels less than 120mg/dL or 90-140mg/dL
Pulmonary function tests demonstrating persistent obstruction or incompletely reversible airflow obstruction after aggressive bronchodilator treatment
Clinical documentation of emphysema, COPD, or asthma
Documentation of unexplained liver disease, including obstructive liver disease in infancy
Documentation of identifiable risk factors such as cigarette smoking or occupational exposure
Documentation of sibling relationship to an individual with AATD
Results of prior targeted mutation analysis or PI typing if requesting SERPINA1 sequence analysis
Documentation of discrepancies between clinical presentation, serum AAT quantification, targeted mutation analysis, and/or PI typing if requesting SERPINA1 sequence analysis
Verification that the rendering laboratory is a qualified provider of service per the Health Plan policy
